source.title: Working Memory: Delay Activity, Yes! Persistent Activity? Maybe Not

confidence_rationale: The explicit adjudication of the fork. Lundqvist, Herman & Miller argue the standard 'persistent spiking' picture is largely an artifact of averaging spikes across time and trials; single-trial activity occurs in sparse transient gamma bursts, and information is carried BETWEEN spikes by short-term synaptic plasticity ('impressions left in the network'). Delay activity is a WM mechanism, but it is sparse, not persistent. Resolves the autopsy's A-vs-B fork toward B (with sparse bursty reactivation), and underwrites both CRF prescriptions: activity-decoupled maintenance + a non-per-tick-firing readout.
failure_signatures: Trial-and-time-averaged firing creates an ILLUSION of continuous persistent activity that disappears on single trials (sparse bursts). A maintenance readout built on smoothed/aggregate activity (or on per-tick active fraction) inherits this artifact and misreads sparse-but-maintained as either continuous or absent.

If information is carried between spikes by synaptic 'impressions', then any activity-based availability accounting necessarily under-counts maintained-but-silent rules -- exactly the crf_frac_active 0.016 collapse in the differentiated regime.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Delay activity is a working-memory mechanism, but the evidence for CONTINUOUS persistent spiking is largely an artifact of averaging across time and trials. On single trials, delay activity occurs in sparse, transient (gamma) bursts; between bursts, information is retained by short-term synaptic plasticity -- 'spikes leave an impression in the networks that maintains WM information between spiking.' Memory is held by temporary changes in synaptic weights during the quiescent periods.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the head-on answer to the V3-EXQ-666 fork. The biologically-correct picture is NOT 'keep every available rule firing' (naive fork A) and NOT a binary fork B either -- it is sparse, bursty reactivation riding on a silent synaptic store. For the CRF: maintain a differentiated rule's availability as a persistent synaptic-trace ('impression') that survives silence; let it be refreshed/reactivated by occasional matches (the bursts); and DO NOT measure maintenance by per-tick firing. crf_frac_active is precisely the averaged-activity artifact this paper warns against: a sparsely-maintained rule reads as ~0 active fraction yet is fully available.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A perspective/review article (argument from re-interpreting existing data), not a new experiment; the burst-coding account, while well-supported by the authors' LFP/spiking work, remains debated against strong-persistent-activity proponents (e.g. Constantinidis et al. 2018, the paired commentary). The CRF should adopt the activity-silent-plus-sparse-reactivation FORM without asserting the burst-vs-persistent debate is fully closed in biology.
mapping.source_context: Perspective/review, macaque PFC working memory; integrates the authors' gamma/beta-burst LFP findings (Lundqvist et al. 2016, Neuron) with the synaptic-trace WM literature.

confidence_components.notes: High mapping_fidelity: the paper's central warning (averaged activity hides sparse-but-maintained coding) is a direct diagnosis of the crf_frac_active readout failure. source_quality strong-for-a-perspective but it is argument-from-reinterpretation, and the burst account is contested -> not at ceiling. transfer_risk low-moderate.
